# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** 76 years old  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c16 P15](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>; Jim Boyd  <sub>[v4 c22 P17](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0017), [v4 c24 P11](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is a tall, ungainly, somewhat stooped man, yet he suggests great strength and endurance. He has a clean-shaven face deeply lined and bronzed, a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, and remarkably blue, deep-set eyes. He is outwardly homely, with spare jaws, a rugged mouth, and a square brow.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015)_

## Personality

He is a high-souled, simple-minded, and cheerful man who possesses an unshakeable placidity and hospitality. A passionate worshipper of beauty, every lovely sight or sound brings him subtle inner joy, though he lamentably lacks outward comeliness himself. He possesses a quaint wisdom, eternal youth in his heart, and a chronic habit of enjoying life.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

## Goals

- To see his life-book published  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c28 P35](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0035)</sub>

## History

At sixteen, Captain Jim formed a close friendship with John Selwyn, the Glen schoolmaster who taught him a lifelong love of poetry. Driven by a sea-going heritage, he ran off to sea and spent most of his life sailing the world before retiring five years prior to keep the lighthouse at Four Winds Point. During his sea-faring years, he lost his beloved sweetheart Margaret when her dory drifted out to sea during a storm. In a Havana boarding house, he discovered an amnesiac Dick Moore and returned him to his wife Leslie. In his elder years, he kept the Four Winds light alongside his nephew Alec and welcomed Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe to the shore, quickly becoming a beloved friend and companion. He shared his life-book of experiences with visiting author Owen Ford, who collaborated with him to turn it into a published book. After seeing the book accepted and watching Anne and Gilbert name their son after him, Captain Jim peacefully passed away.

_Sources: [v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009), [v4 c6 P19](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0019), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c28 P35](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0035), [v4 c34 P23](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0023), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Descended from a line of sea-going relatives on his mother's side  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Fell asleep in a garden at eight years old and was comforted by the moon  <sub>[v4 c7 P63](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0063)</sub>
- Ran off to sea as a young man after schoolmaster John Selwyn married  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048)</sub>
- Lost his sweetheart Margaret at sea over fifty years prior  <sub>[v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016)</sub>
- Found Dick Moore suffering from memory loss in a Havana boarding house and brought him home  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>
- Rescued his golden cat, the First Mate  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>
- Never had children of his own  <sub>[v4 c34 P18](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0018)</sub>

## Quotes

> ‘Captain Jim’ is my week-a-day name and you might as well begin as you’re sartain to end up—calling me that.  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

> You’re young and I’m old, but our souls are about the same age, I reckon. We both belong to the race that knows Joseph, as Cornelia Bryant would say.  <sub>[v4 c7 P54](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0054)</sub>

> I saved his life, and when you’ve saved a creature’s life you’re bound to love it. It’s next thing to giving life.  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>

> I’ve kind of contracted a habit of enj’ying things. It’s got so chronic that I believe I even enj’y the disagreeable things.  <sub>[v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)</sub>

> I don’t think I’m a coward, Mistress Blythe—I’ve looked an ugly death in the face more than once without blenching. But the thought of a lingering death does give me a queer, sick feeling of horror.  <sub>[v4 c35 P36](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0036)</sub>
